scenario_description:
Objective: Avoid rainwater accumulating in the cockpit because a cure cover remains over drains before an overnight storm.
Emerging Need: Supply purchase and cure timing alone only preserve a finish; the risk appears when offsite absence, a heavy-rain alert, and a brief dockside availability window align.
Decision Context: Observable updates establish timing, weather, and feasibility, while the service workpad holds the cover-specific scupper hazard, cockpit-only access limit, and no-cost preparation constraint.
Consequence: Timely attention can keep drainage open before the storm; once the nearby helper leaves and the overnight work block continues, the preventive window has passed.

parameter.description: Offsite museum install block; carpool leaves Tacoma at 13:00 Tuesday and returns Wednesday morning.

parameter.subject: Heavy Rain Warning for Tacoma waterfront tonight
parameter.body: A heavy-rain warning is in effect for the Tacoma waterfront from 19:00 Tuesday through 06:00 Wednesday. Expected totals are 2.4 to 3.1 inches with strongest rates after 21:00. Small-craft and liveaboard owners should confirm cockpit drains and deck scuppers are clear before evening rain bands arrive.

parameter.content: My marina errand landed on B-dock from about 17:50 to 18:10, then I’m heading straight to the ferry and won’t have signal for the rest of the night.
I’m off B-dock and boarding the ferry now. I didn’t stop at your cockpit, and I won’t be back in Tacoma until late tomorrow.
